artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan for lean-comparator-run.sh: design record and clean-room trust chain, runner skeleton with an 8-value verdict vocabulary, clean-room/config synthesis, sandboxed guard-serialised invocation, stderr-based verdict classification, fixtures, regression suite, and manifest wiring with an honest deferred-criteria report.

memory_candidates.content: Shared build-guard / caching wrappers whose result-sharing key is a hash of the wrapped command's ARGUMENT VECTOR are unsafe for any call site whose behaviour is determined by the CONTENT of a file named by a constant path argument. lake-build-guard.sh's scope_key hashes `env <binary> <config.json>` (the path, not the body) and its tree fingerprint covers *.lean/lakefile/lean-toolchain but not config.json -- so two runs differing only in a JSON config's body are indistinguishable and a stale REPLAY returns the wrong answer. Before reusing a shared guard at a new call site, ask what determines the wrapped command's output and check that ALL of it is in either the cache key or the fingerprint; if not, pass --no-share (a correctness requirement, not a performance choice) or fold a content hash into argv. Do not copy a sibling call site's flag set without this check -- the sibling may be safe only because its output is fully determined by the fingerprinted tree.
